thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: autoscaler-surge detected for gpu-pool-us-west-2. 90th p99 latency spike on /v1/generate, error rate 12%. Runbook: <https://redwood.runbooks/infra/autoscale-surge|autoscale-surge>

Alice K.: I’m oncall. Looking at metrics now. Which customers are impacted?

Ravi P.: Topline: sustained scaling churn for the gpu pool over the last 6m. Autoscaler oscillation created temporary shortage — several queued inference batches were dropped and we fell back to slower CPU hosts. Telemetry: https://telemetry.redwood/gpu-pools/us-west-2/surge

Maya S.: Confirmed. I can bump the dedicated pool manually and drain noncritical jobs. Suggest: +2 GPUs, disable batch-worker-low for 10m, and trigger a regional failover to eu-west as needed.

Jorge L.: I’ll pause low-priority retrains and evict preemption-friendly jobs. Doing now.

Lena C.: CS: We have two paying customers with >95th percentile errors. Notified both with a short note, asking if they are seeing application-level errors. I’ll escalate to enterprise ops if they report production impact.

Nikhil R.: FYI oncall handoff happening in ~20m — if this is still hot, stay attached.

Alice K.: Action plan: 1) Manual scale +2 to gpu-pool-us-west-2 2) Toggle batch-worker-low off 3) Adjust autoscaler cooldown from 60s -> 180s 4) Add temporary routing to eu-west-1 for 10% of traffic. Doing 1-2 now.

Maya S.: Manual scale command:```sh
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/gpu-pool-us-west-2 --replicas=6
# confirm nodes: kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-us-west-2
```
Scaling started — ETA ~90s.

incident-bot: Scaling event: gpu-pool-us-west-2 replicas increased to 6 by maya.s at 1710567955.

Ravi P.: While scaling, I’m going to increase autoscaler stable-window to avoid flip-flopping:
```yaml
policy:
  cooldown: 180s
  scale_up_limit: 2
  scale_down_limit: 1
```
I’ll push that in 2m.

Jorge L.: batch-worker-low stopped. Evicted ~120 low-priority jobs. Queue length down to 300 -> 80.

Alice K.: Latency trending down. p95 20% -> 8% within 3m. Error rate 12% -> 2.3%. Still some tail.

Lena C.: Customer A (acme-analytics) says errors reduced but still seeing slow responses for some large requests. They want a post-incident note.

Maya S.: Can we set a short-lived model-fallback for large requests to smaller-quantized variants? That will reduce CPU fallback impact.

Ravi P.: Yes. We have model alias fallback: v1-large -> v1-medium-quant. I can flip rule for 15m. Doing it now.

incident-bot: Routing change: model-alias fallback applied for 15 minutes by ravi.p at 1710568120.

Alice K.: That change dropped CPU fallback latency significantly. Good interim mitigation. Continuing to monitor.

Nikhil R.: Handoff: I’ll join for the next 30m to capture notes and handle any paging. If things are stable by then I’ll start the postmortem scheduling.

Jorge L.: Observed a small preemption spike on node g4-84 at 1710568250 — likely unrelated but noted.

Alice K.: Okay, we’re in steady state. Primary mitigations done. Next: remediation items and postmortem.

Alice K.: Proposed post-incident timeline: postmortem doc in 48h, follow-up meeting tomorrow 10:00 PT, assign owners for fixes. Who can lead remediation tracking?

Maya S.: I’ll own the infra tuning ticket (AUTOSCALE-2345). Deliverables: autoscaler config audit, test harness for oscillation, and a canary script for cool-down changes. Target: 2 weeks.

Ravi P.: I’ll own routing and fallback improvements (ROUTE-778). Deliverables: improve model fallback priority, automated minor-region spillover, and an emergency runbook for manual scaling. Target: next sprint (1 week).

Jorge L.: I’ll take preemption resilience work (SCHED-442). Deliverables: job priority tagging, eviction thresholds, and capacity reservations for critical paths. Target: 3 weeks.

Lena C.: I’ll draft the customer-facing incident note and coordinate with legal for enterprise customers. Deliverable: initial note within 4 hours, detailed follow-up after postmortem.

Alice K.: Creating tracking issue now: INF-2026 (link: https://tickets.redwood/INF-2026).

Alice K.: Quick list of action items (assignments & rough due dates):
- Maya S.: autoscaler config audit + test harness (AUTOSCALE-2345) — due 2026-03-29
- Ravi P.: automated regional spillover & fallback rules (ROUTE-778) — due 2026-03-22
- Jorge L.: job-priority + eviction policies (SCHED-442) — due 2026-04-05
- Lena C.: customer notification drafts + enterprise follow-ups — due 2026-03-16
- Alice K.: write initial postmortem skeleton & schedule review meeting — due 2026-03-16

Maya S.: Adding a small acceptance test to CI that simulates flapping scale events and verifies stable-window prevents oscillation. Pseudocode:```py
# simulate metrics
for t in range(0, 600):
  metrics = base + random_spike(t)
  autoscaler.step(metrics)
assert not autoscaler.oscillated()
```

Ravi P.: Also adding an alert refinement: split autoscaler-oscillation into S1 (minor) and S0 (major) with paging to oncall only for S0. That should reduce noise.

incident-bot: Postmortem meeting scheduled by alice.k for 2026-03-16T17:00:00Z. Link: https://calendar.redwood/meetings/INF-2026-postmortem

Alice K.: Note for postmortem: capture exact timeline of queue drops, fallback events, model fallback activation times, and customer impact window. Bring logs: autoscaler logs, router logs, telemetry snapshots.

Lena C.: Customer note sent (short form). Waiting for replies. Will escalate if they confirm production errors.

Nikhil R.: I’ll own the incident timeline and ensure the postmortem doc collects raw artifacts.

Jorge L.: Scheduled a short follow-up runbook update session for tomorrow 09:30 PT to codify the manual steps we took.

Alice K.: Thanks all. Marking thread as stable. I’ll update INF-2026 with owners and copy action items. If anything regress, ping @oncall. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated - monitoring. Created postmortem stub INF-2026 at 1710569799.

Alice K.: Closing notes: remember to add metrics dashboards for model-fallback impact (tokens/sec, cpu-fallback-rate). Also add an SLA check for critical customers when fallback triggers.

Maya S.: Will add dashboards and a synthetic test that exercises large requests against quantized variants.

Ravi P.: Will PR autoscaler cooldown change to canary channel and run chaos tests.

Lena C.: Will follow up with customer A/enterprise ops and post a summary in #customer-impact.

Jorge L.: Thanks team.

Alice K.: Great work — nice calm firefight. Postmortem and tickets will be source of truth for remediation.

(End of thread)
